capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: In Restricted Mode, Connect Codex does not write the project config: checking that git will not commit the token means running git in the workspace, which runs the repository's own hooks. The `codex mcp add` command is offered instead.
configuration.focusLockIndicator.enabled: Enable/disable the floating indicator that shows when focused in the AI browser.
configuration.useIntegratedBrowser.descr: Open URLs in VS Code's built-in browser rather than the AI Browser webview panel. The built-in browser is what the element-picker commands attach to, and it supports clipboard shortcuts, find in page and DevTools that the panel cannot. Turn it off only if you specifically want the panel.
configuration.searchEngine.description: Search engine used when the address bar input is a search term rather than a URL. Set to 'none' to disable address bar search.

configuration.mcp.enabled.description: Run a local MCP server so Claude Code, Codex and VS Code chat can drive the integrated browser. It listens on loopback only and requires a per-workspace token.
configuration.mcp.port.description: First port to try for the MCP server. Left unset, each window derives its own first choice from the workspace path, within the 20 ports starting here, so a window keeps the same port across restarts and a saved config does not go stale. Set it explicitly and the window starts exactly here instead. Either way it walks on until it finds a free one.

configuration.updateCheck.enabled.descri: Look for new releases of AI Browser in the [repository](https://github.com/Denis-Davidoff/vs-code-tab-browser-ultimate) and show a notification when one is out. This extension is installed from a VSIX, so nothing else updates it. Once it has reached GitHub it waits six hours before asking again; it announces each release once, and says nothing when there is no update.

configuration.logins.enabled.description: Save logins and passkeys for pages in the integrated browser, in VS Code's secret storage (encrypted by the operating system: Keychain, DPAPI or the Secret Service). On Linux with no keyring available, VS Code keeps secrets in memory only, per window, so they are gone when the window closes. Turned off, nothing is injected into pages, nothing is offered or filled, and passkeys are off — saved logins can still be managed, exported and imported.
configuration.logins.offerToSave.descrip: After a sign-in that went through, offer to save the login, or to update a saved password that changed. The offer is a status bar item; nothing covers the page.
configuration.logins.showSuggestions.des: Show a status bar item while the page in front of you has a sign-in form and a login is saved for it. `Cmd+Shift+L` / `Ctrl+Shift+L` fills either way.
Fill a sign-in form as soon as it appears, when exactly one login is saved for that exact address and the fields are empty. Off by default: a page then receives your password without you asking.
configuration.passkeys.enabled.descripti: Sign in with passkeys stored in AI Browser, and save new ones a site creates. Every passkey ceremony in the page asks you first, and the tab's own authenticators (a security key, a phone) are reached by choosing "Use a security key or another device" in that prompt. A frame from another site, such as an embedded payment confirmation or sign-in widget, is not reached: its ceremony gets no prompt and fails after its own timeout while this is on. Turning this off hands those back to the browser.
